title: Policy-driven archive-to-redact pipeline and cert-token service
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Deliver an automated pipeline that translates declarative tenant retention rules into a staged workflow: archive -> redact -> certify -> purge. Provide a lightweight certificate token service (signed tokens) and a forensic evidence snapshotter that can produce tamper-evident artifacts for customer audits. The pipeline should support dry-run simulation, per-tenant policy overrides, cross-region shadow runs for residency verification, and an operator UI to inspect, pause, and replay deletion DAGs.
acceptance_criteria: Retention rule interpreter accepts policy objects and produces a deterministic DAG of actions (archive, transform(redact), certify, purge)
Archive step materializes immutable snapshots in configured storage (region-aware) and records checksums in the evidence ledger
Redact step applies configurable transformers (regex, PII classifier, redaction templates) with policy-level audit logs
Cert-token service issues signed certificates (JWT) that include: action hashed snapshot, timestamp, region, operator-id, and signature from KMS/HSM-backed key
Evidence snapshot API returns a compressed, tamper-evident bundle and a verification endpoint for customers with signed cert-token
Dry-run mode simulates all steps, outputs expected diffs, and does not alter production data
Operator UI surface shows per-tenant DAG, step-level status, ability to pause/resume/cancel, and links to evidence bundles and cert-tokens
Cross-region shadow-run verifies that deletion effects are observable in the tenant's residency region without performing destructive operations there (read-only verification)
End-to-end tests exercising policy permutations (time-based retention, explicit user-initiated forget, legal hold interaction) pass in CI with mocked storage and KMS
Telemetry emitted for each step: latency, token issuance success, evidence bundle size, and any transform failures
notes: Design tradeoff: we prefer signed cert-tokens (short-lived) over long-term customer-facing receipts to limit surface area of stored secrets. Tokens are verifiable via public key endpoints.
We will reuse existing evidence-ledger schema where possible but add a 'snapshot_manifest_v2' with a hash chain and region stamp.
Operator UI mockups are in Drive (link below). Initial plan targets Hosted + Dedicated; Private will require additional KMS/HSM integration work.

Performance: archiving and snapshotting should be backgrounded and rate-limited per tenant to avoid noisy neighbor effects on Dedicated pools. Suggested default throttle: 500 MB/min per tenant with config override.
